children: By Trixie Yap, Jeslyn Lerh and Mohi Narayan

Oil product stocks held in Asia's key fuel trading hub Singapore were at slightly more than two-month highs, government data released on Thursday showed, tracking the rise in light and middle distillates stocks.
Combined onshore oil product inventories were at 40.47 million barrels in the week ended September 9, data from Enterprise Singapore showed, compared with 39.04 million barrels a week earlier.
September exports in the Asia region are likely to stay robust for diesel and jet fuel, though they may slow for gasoline due to margin concerns, multiple trade sources said this week.
However, markets were still broadly pricing in continuously low global fuel inventories, with diesel being the major concern for some regions in the West.
MIDDLE, LIGHT DISTILLATES STOCKS GAIN
Middle distillates stocks went back up to above 8 million barrels, tracking a decline in jet fuel and kerosene net exports.
Jet fuel and kerosene net exports fell 11% from a week ago, with imports from China continuing for a second straight week.
Diesel and gasoil net exports, however, rose by more than 30 times from a week earlier as imports fell nearly 80% over the same period.
Imports of the industrial and transport fuel were mostly from Malaysia and China, while exports mostly headed to the Pacific Island regions and Malaysia.
Light distillates stocks, including naphtha and gasoline, rose to a one-month high of 11.87 million barrels.
Gasoline imports totalled about 185,000 metric tons (approximately 1.6 million barrels) during the period, while exports reached roughly 390,000 tons.

Outbound gasoline volumes were led by Malaysia at about 100,000 tons, followed by Indonesia at around 71,000 tons. Gasoline inflows were led by South Korea at nearly 99,000 tons, followed by China at about 52,000 tons.
Naphtha imports stood at about 206,000 tons (approximately 1.8 million barrels), led by Russia at nearly 89,000 tons, followed by India at around 36,000 tons.
Singapore exported about 34,000 tons of naphtha, with all shipments destined for China.
RESIDUAL FUEL STOCKS AT TWO-WEEK LOW
Residual fuel oil inventories dipped slightly to a two-week low, with imports more than halving.
Stockpiles were down 0.5% week on week at 20.36 million barrels (3.21 million tons), the data showed.
Imports of fuel oil dropped over 50% to about 451,000 tons. India became the top supplier of volumes for the week, with refiners exporting supplies steadily via tenders in recent weeks.
Other key suppliers included Brazil and Mexico as traders pulled arbitrage cargoes over.
Meanwhile, exports of fuel oil climbed 4.5% week on week, reaching 155,000 tons. Bangladesh and China were the key outlets.
